title: Yuvilab English learning unit
description: The authoring contract for a hand-written English unit under backend/content/english/units/. It is checked by scripts/check_english_content.py, never at runtime: the player and the catalog stay deliberately forgiving so a content mistake degrades one screen instead of failing a lesson. This file is where a mistake is supposed to be caught. Every object is closed (additionalProperties: false) on purpose — a typo like 'presentaion' or 'correctAnswer' would otherwise be silently ignored, which is exactly how the twelve kind-less items got shipped.

learningObjective.description: The goal this unit serves. Absent only on a sub-topic summary unit, which by 720 §3.4 has no goal of its own.

prerequisiteLearningObjective.description: Goals that must come first. An array even when empty, because the catalog treats a unit with no prerequisites and a unit whose prerequisites are unknown identically.

contentId.description: Dotted id. Must survive being pasted into an xAPI object IRI, so no spaces and no characters that would need escaping.

trilingual.description: Learner-facing text. All three locales are required — a missing one renders as an empty screen for that sector, not as a fallback.

kataTitles.description: Unit titles keyed by Kata's language LABELS rather than locale codes — this is the provider's spelling and `kata_client.title_translations` is what maps it to he/ar/en. Do not 'fix' it to locale codes: the same reader parses real Kata units.

supportText.description: Scaffolding shown to a learner who is stuck. Hebrew and Arabic are required because it talks ABOUT the English on screen; English is optional and only worth writing when the tip is itself about pronunciation or wording.

media.description: One image. It is AUTHORED as a `prompt` plus `alt`, and `scripts/generate_unit_images.py` fills in `src`/`srcset`/`width`/`height` — so the picture is described in the content and the file is a build artefact of it. `alt` is required in all three languages because the picture may BE the question (image MCQ), and a learner on a screen reader who loses it loses the item, not a decoration. `width`/`height` come with any `src` so the box is reserved before the bytes arrive and nothing shifts under a tapping finger. The check script fails a unit whose images have not been generated yet.

src.description: Path under content/english/assets/, relative to that directory. Content-hashed by the generator, so it is safe to serve immutable.

prompt.description: AUTHORING ONLY — the text the image was generated from. Stripped from the player payload; kept here so a regeneration is reproducible and so a reviewer can see what was asked for.

order.description: Route position. Two components MAY share one order — that is how an equivalent alternative representation is declared (720 §3.2).

recommendedAfterFail.description: Where a failing learner goes next. Every id here must name a component in a DIFFERENT representation — re-serving the same screens is what 720 §3.3 forbids, and the check script verifies the media format actually changes.

item.description: One screen — a פריט, 'the unit of interaction that can be recorded as a single event'. Not one question: a screen may carry several.

informationToBot.description: Server-only teaching notes for the coach: the goal, the common misconceptions, and what may NOT be said. Never reaches the browser.

presentation.description: What the screen shows before it asks anything. `kind` is required: the player tolerates its absence, but an author who omits it silently gets a bare prompt with no body, which is how twelve screens shipped degraded.

lines.description: The text, one tappable line at a time. A plain string is a paragraph; the object form says what the line IS, because a real invitation has a title, a notice has fields, and a chat has speakers — and rendering all of those as identical grey paragraphs is what made these screens look like a wall of shouting.

role.description: heading — a title. field — `LABEL: value` from a form or notice. speaker — `Name: message` in a conversation. divider — a rule between two parts of a document, and the one role that carries no text and is never read aloud.

referenceText.description: What the learner is asked to say. An array gives one practice button per sentence; a single string is one continuous stretch, which is how a 'say it in one go' screen is authored. The player accepts both.

source.description: The text being mediated FROM. Hebrew and Arabic, because it is the learner's own language and English is what they are carrying it into — an English version would remove the task. Both are required: this text once existed in one language per component, which made the after-fail alternative and the other sector the same thing, and routed a Hebrew learner into an Arabic notice they could not read.

labelledChoices.description: Options the learner picks for themselves — a reflection answer or a self-check. Never graded, so there is no key. It must be an ARRAY: the player reads `.length` to decide whether to draw the block at all, so a bare trilingual string here does not render as a question, it renders as nothing.

id.description: Stable across translations — it is what the reflection answer is recorded as, so renaming it orphans the history.

questionId.description: MUST be q1, q2, … — the xAPI object id ends in this, and both our analytics and Kata's parse it with ^q(\d+)$. Any other spelling makes the answer invisible to the LRS.

questionType.description: NOTE the trap: `fill-in` is a sentence with a blank whose answer is CHOSEN from options — it renders as multiple choice. Free typing is `text-entry`. An image MCQ is not a type at all: it is `single-choice` plus `image`/`answerMedia`.

image.description: A picture the question is about — the scene in an image MCQ.

answers.description: The options offered. Empty for `text-entry`, where there is nothing to choose from.

answerMedia.description: Keyed by the answer string it illustrates, so picture options stay in step with `answers` even when they are reordered.

prompts.description: The left-hand side of a matching question — what gets paired TO an answer.

correctAnswers.description: The key. NEVER leaves the server. Choice types: exactly one, and it must be one of `answers`. `match`: one `promptId=answer` string per prompt. `text-entry`: every spelling that should be accepted.

feedback.description: Words, never a score. The incorrect branch must explain the error or give a strategy — and must not give the answer away (720 §feedback).

answers.description: Kept for shape compatibility with every consumer that reads `answers`, but there is nothing to offer.
